provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Art: landscape painting
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the primary colours needed for painting.
The pupils should be able to mix natural colours from primary colours.
Introduction:
We have learned about basic colour theory. Today we will apply this knowledge to create landscape paintings using natural colours.
Content:
Landscape painting shows natural scenes like mountains, rivers, and trees. To paint a landscape, we need a palette with colours like green for plants, blue for sky, and brown for soil. Natural colours come from things around us. For example, green leaves can make green paint, red soil can make brown paint. We mix primary colours-red, yellow, blue-to get secondary colours. Yellow and blue make green. Red and yellow make orange. Blue and red make purple. We can add water to make lighter shades.
Class activity:
Each pupil will create a simple landscape painting using at least three mixed colours from their palette.
Evaluation questions:
What are the three primary colours?
How do we make green paint?
Name one natural material that can be used to make paint.
Summary:
Today we learned how to mix natural colours for landscape painting using primary colours.

topics.title: Music: harmony basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing a simple two-part song.
The pupils should be able to explain what a round is in music.
Introduction:
We have practiced singing alone. Today we will learn how to sing together in harmony.
Content:
Harmony is when different notes are sung at the same time to create a pleasing sound. In two-part singing, one group sings the main melody while another group sings a different note that fits well together. A round is a type of song where groups start singing the same melody at different times. Like when we sing 'Row Row Row Your Boat' and one group starts first, then another group starts after a few lines. This creates harmony as different groups sing different parts of the same song at the same time.
Class activity:
The class will be divided into two groups to practice singing a simple Nigerian folk song in two parts.
Evaluation questions:
What is harmony in music?
How many parts are in two-part singing?
Describe how a round song is sung.
Summary:
Today we learned about harmony through two-part singing and round singing.

topics.title: Art: graphic design
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify key elements of a good poster.
The pupils should be able to design a sports poster with appropriate visuals.
Introduction:
We have looked at different types of art. Today we will learn how to create posters and flyers that communicate messages effectively.
Content:
Graphic design is about creating visual communication like posters and flyers. A good poster has a clear message, attractive images, and easy-to-read text. For a sports poster, we need pictures of sports equipment or athletes, the name of the event, date, time, and place. We use bright colours to grab attention. We can draw footballs, basketballs, or athletes running. The text should be big and easy to read from far away. We arrange elements so the most important information stands out.
Class activity:
Each pupil will create a poster for a fictional school sports day including date, time, venue, and appropriate sports imagery.
Evaluation questions:
Name three important elements of a good poster.
What information should be on a sports poster?
Why do we use bright colours in posters?
Summary:
Today we learned how to design effective posters and created sports posters with proper elements.

topics.title: Music: music technology
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what digital beats are.
The pupils should be able to create a simple musical loop using classroom objects.
Introduction:
We have made music with our voices and instruments. Today we will explore how technology helps us create music.
Content:
Music technology uses electronic devices to create and change sounds. Digital beats are rhythmic patterns made using computers or special machines. Like the drum machine that plays different drum sounds. A loop is a short piece of music that repeats over and over. We can make a simple loop by repeating a pattern of sounds. For example, clap-stomp-clap-stomp repeated many times. In modern Nigerian music, artists use digital beats to create songs like the ones we hear on the radio.
Class activity:
Groups will create a four-beat pattern using classroom objects and repeat it to make a loop.
Evaluation questions:
What are digital beats?
What is a musical loop?
Name one modern Nigerian song that uses digital beats.
Summary:
Today we learned about music technology and created simple loops using everyday sounds.

topics.title: Art: architecture
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify features of Nigerian buildings.
The pupils should be able to draw and label their dream house.
Introduction:
We have studied different types of paintings. Today we will learn about buildings and how to design them.
Content:
Architecture is the art of designing buildings. Nigerian buildings have special features like flat roofs for hot weather, large windows for ventilation, and courtyards for family gatherings. Traditional houses might have mud walls and thatched roofs. Modern buildings use concrete and have different shapes. When we draw a house, we need to show the front, doors, windows, roof, and maybe some surrounding elements like trees or a fence. We use simple shapes like rectangles for walls, triangles for roofs, and squares for windows.
Class activity:
Each pupil will draw their dream house with at least three special features and label them.
Evaluation questions:
Name two features of Nigerian buildings.
What shapes do we use to draw a simple house?
Describe your dream house.
Summary:
Today we learned about Nigerian architecture and designed our dream houses.

topics.title: Drama: stage craft
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the purpose of stage lighting.
The pupils should be able to participate in a simple stage crew practice.
Introduction:
We have learned about acting. Today we will learn about what happens behind the scenes in a play.
Content:
Stage craft includes all the technical parts of a play like sets, lighting, and sound. The set is the background and furniture on stage that makes the play look real. Lighting helps create mood-bright lights for happy scenes, dim lights for scary scenes. Sound effects make the play more exciting like thunder during a storm or birds singing in a forest. A stage crew helps move sets, control lights, and play sounds during the performance. Like in our school play, someone needs to turn the lights on and off at the right time.
Class activity:
The class will be divided into small groups to practice different stage crew tasks like setting up a simple scene and operating sound effects.
Evaluation questions:
What is the purpose of stage lighting?
Name two elements of stage craft.
What does the stage crew do during a performance?
Summary:
Today we learned about stage craft and practiced different behind-the-scenes roles.

topics.title: Art: ceramics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the coil method of pottery.
The pupils should be able to identify the purpose of glazing.
Introduction:
We have made drawings and paintings. Today we will learn how to create objects using clay.
Content:
Ceramics is the art of making objects from clay. The coil method involves rolling clay into long ropes and coiling them to build a shape. Like making a pot by stacking clay circles on top of each other. After shaping, we let the clay dry. Then we fire it in a special hot oven called a kiln to make it hard and strong. Glazing is adding a special liquid to clay objects before firing that makes them shiny and waterproof. Like the colourful plates and cups we use at home. Traditional Nigerian pottery includes clay pots for storing water and bowls for eating.
Class activity:
Each pupil will create a small clay object using the coil method and decorate it with patterns.
Evaluation questions:
Describe the coil method of pottery.
Why do we fire clay objects?
What is glazing used for?
Summary:
Today we learned about ceramics and created clay objects using the coil method.

topics.title: Music: performance polish
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate good stage presence.
The pupils should be able to explain proper microphone technique.
Introduction:
We have practiced singing songs. Today we will learn how to perform them well on stage.
Content:
Stage presence is how performers act and move on stage to engage the audience. Good stage presence includes standing tall, making eye contact, and showing confidence. Like when our favourite musician performs at a concert and moves around the stage. Proper microphone technique involves holding the mic close to your mouth but not touching it, and adjusting distance based on volume. When singing softly, hold it closer. When singing loudly, hold it farther away. This prevents loud noises and feedback. Like the way news presenters on TV use microphones.
Class activity:
Pairs will practice performing a short song for the class while focusing on stage presence and microphone technique.
Evaluation questions:
What is stage presence?
How should you hold a microphone when singing softly?
Why is good posture important for performers?
Summary:
Today we learned about performance polish and practiced good stage presence and microphone technique.

topics.title: Dance: contemporary moves
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify two different dance styles.
The pupils should be able to perform a short group dance routine.
Introduction:
We have learned about traditional Nigerian dances. Today we will explore modern dance styles.
Content:
Contemporary dance is a modern style that combines different dance forms. It can include elements from traditional Nigerian dances, hip-hop, ballet, and other styles. Like when dancers mix the Agba dance with modern moves. Blending styles means taking movements from different dances and putting them together in new ways. For a group routine, we need to coordinate movements so everyone dances at the same time. We can create simple patterns like moving in a circle or forming lines and then changing formations.
Class activity:
The class will learn and practice a short contemporary dance routine combining at least two different styles.
Evaluation questions:
What is contemporary dance?
Name two dance styles that can be blended.
Why is coordination important in group dancing?
Summary:
Today we learned about contemporary dance and practiced blending styles in a group routine.

topics.title: Revision and showcase
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to present their best art work.
The pupils should be able to perform in a class concert.
Introduction:
We have learned many things this term. Today we will share what we have created and learned with the class.
Content:
A showcase is when we display our best work and perform for others. For our art showcase, we will display our landscape paintings, graphic designs, architecture drawings, and ceramic objects. Each pupil will choose their best piece to show and explain what they made. For the class concert, we will perform the songs we learned in music class and the dance routines we practiced. We need to speak clearly when explaining our work and perform with confidence. Like when artists show their work in galleries or musicians perform at concerts.
Class activity:
The class will organize an exhibition of their art work followed by a performance of music and dance pieces they have learned this term.
Evaluation questions:
What is a showcase?
Why is it important to explain your art work?
What will you perform in the class concert?
Summary:
Today we shared our best work and performed in our class showcase and concert.
